competencies.text: Describe climate change. Explain biological responses to climate change.
Explain climate change impacts on Philippine ecosystems.

days.title: Climate Change & Life
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe climate change, explain how organisms respond biologically to changing climate, and describe the impacts of climate change on Philippine ecosystems.

🌏 What Is Climate Change?

Climate change refers to long-term shifts in global or regional temperature, precipitation, wind patterns, and other climate indicators over decades or centuries.

Weather is short-term (today, this week). Climate is long-term (decades, centuries).

AspectWeatherClimate
Time scaleHours to daysDecades to centuries
Example

ChangesFrequentlySlowly over long periods

🔥 Causes of Climate Change

While natural factors (volcanic eruptions, solar cycles) affect climate, human activities since the Industrial Revolution are the dominant cause of recent warming:

  • Burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, natural gas) for electricity and transportation releases CO₂.
  • Deforestation (especially in tropical forests) removes carbon sinks.
  • Agriculture releases methane (CH₄) from livestock and rice paddies.
  • Industrial processes release CO₂ and other greenhouse gases (GHGs).

These gases trap heat in the atmosphere — the enhanced greenhouse effect.

🌡️ Observed Changes in the Philippines

  • Rising temperatures — average temperatures have increased, especially in urban areas.
  • More intense typhoons — stronger, wetter, and less predictable storms.
  • Sea-level rise — threatens coastal communities and freshwater supplies.
  • More frequent droughts and floods — El Niño and La Niña events intensify.
  • Coral bleaching — reefs die when water temperature rises even 1–2°C above normal.

🐟 Biological Responses to Climate Change

ResponseWhat HappensExample
Range shiftsSpecies move toward cooler areas (higher elevation or latitude)Fish species moving to deeper, cooler waters
Phenology shiftsTiming of life events changesBirds nesting earlier; plants flowering sooner
AdaptationSpecies evolve or adjust to new conditionsCoral species more tolerant to warmer water survive and reproduce
ExtinctionSpecies unable to adapt or move die outAmphibians highly sensitive to temperature and humidity changes
Migration changesMigration routes and timing shiftWhales and fish follow shifting food sources

🇵🇭 Climate Change Impacts on Philippine Ecosystems

EcosystemImpact
Coral reefsBleaching events kill corals; fish populations decline; affects 60% of Filipinos who depend on fisheries
MangrovesRising sea levels and stronger storms damage mangrove forests; reduces coastal protection
Rice paddiesErratic rainfall, typhoons, and saltwater intrusion reduce yields; threatens food security
ForestsChanges in rainfall patterns shift forest boundaries; more forest fires during droughts
Freshwater lakesWarmer water reduces oxygen; fish kills; algal blooms become more frequent (Laguna de Bay, Taal Lake)
Coastal communitiesSea-level rise forces relocation; loss of homes and livelihoods

🐠 Case Study: Coral Bleaching

Corals are animals that live in partnership with microscopic algae (zooxanthellae). The algae give corals their color and provide food. When water gets too warm:

  1. Corals expel the algae.
  2. They lose their color →

• Without algae, they slowly starve.
  • If temperatures stay high, they die.

    • The Tubbataha Reefs (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) and the Coral Triangle — which includes the Philippines — are hotspots for marine biodiversity and are highly vulnerable.

    🌾 Case Study: Rice & Food Security

    The Philippines is one of the world's largest rice importers. Climate change affects rice through:

    • Typhoons: Destroy crops before harvest.
    • Droughts: Reduce irrigation water.
    • Saltwater intrusion: Makes farmland unusable.
    • Pests: Warmer temperatures expand insect ranges.

    🌱 Why This Matters

    The Philippines is one of the most climate-vulnerable countries in the world. Our geography — an archipelago of over 7,600 islands in the typhoon belt — makes us highly exposed. Understanding climate change is not just science — it's survival.

    📌 Quick Check

    • What is the difference between weather and climate? (Answer: weather is short-term; climate is long-term)
    • What causes coral bleaching? (Answer: warmer water temperature makes corals expel their algae)
    • Name one biological response to climate change. (Answer: range shifts, phenology shifts, adaptation, extinction, migration changes)

days.title: Match Game — Climate Concepts
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each climate concept or impact to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Long-term shifts in temperature, precipitation, and weather patterns
CO₂, methane (CH₄), water vapor — trap heat in the atmosphere
Corals expel their algae when water is too warm, losing color and starving
Threatens coastal Philippine communities and freshwater supplies
Species move to cooler areas — higher elevation or deeper water
Timing of life events changes — birds nesting earlier
Seawater seeps into farmland and aquifers, making them unusable
Human activities increase GHGs and trap more heat than normal

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Philippine Ecosystems
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🐠 A marine biologist diving in Tubbataha Reef notices that corals have lost their bright colors and appear pale white. What is happening?

choices.label: A) The corals are dying from too much sunlight
B) Coral bleaching — warmer water made the corals expel their symbiotic algae
C) The corals are reproducing
D) The corals have been painted white

scenario.text: 🌾 A rice farmer in Nueva Ecija notices that his crop yields have been decreasing over the past 5 years. Typhoons arrive earlier, and dry spells last longer. What is the BEST explanation?

choices.label: A) Climate change is causing more unpredictable and extreme weather patterns
B) He is not using enough fertilizer
C) His farm is too small
D) Rice is no longer profitable

scenario.text: 🦅 A species of bird that used to nest in lowland forests is now nesting at higher elevations. What is the likely cause?

choices.label: A) Rising temperatures have shifted the bird's preferred habitat to cooler higher altitudes — a range shift
B) The birds prefer the view from the mountains
C) The lowland forests are gone
D) The birds are migrating for winter

scenario.text: 🌊 Coastal barangays in La Union are noticing that seawater is reaching further inland during high tides, and wells are becoming salty. What is the PRIMARY cause?

choices.label: A) Sea-level rise due to climate change and over-pumping of groundwater
B) The barangay dug the wells too deep
C) Fishermen are dumping seawater
D) There is no cause — this is normal

scenario.text: 🌿 A farmer plants mangroves along the coastline. How does this help the community?

choices.label: A) Mangroves absorb CO₂ (carbon sink), protect coastlines from storms and erosion, and provide habitat for fish — a natural climate solution
B) Mangroves attract tourists only
C) Mangroves block rainwater
D) Mangroves provide no benefit

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Climate Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Climate Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What is the difference between weather and climate?

choices.label: A) Weather is short-term; climate is long-term
B) Weather is long-term; climate is short-term
C) They are the same thing
D) Weather is about temperature only

escape.text: What is the MAIN cause of recent climate change?

choices.label: A) Human activities releasing greenhouse gases like CO₂ and methane
B) Volcanic eruptions only
C) Solar cycles only
D) Ocean tides

escape.text: What happens to corals when water temperature rises too much?

choices.label: A) They expel their symbiotic algae and bleach, slowly starving
B) They grow faster
C) They change color to red
D) Nothing happens — corals are immune

escape.text: Which of the following is a BIOLOGICAL response to climate change?

choices.label: A) Species shifting to cooler areas (range shift)
B) Building more factories
C) Rising electricity prices
D) Decreasing internet speed

escape.text: Why is the Philippines considered highly vulnerable to climate change?

choices.label: A) It's an archipelago in the typhoon belt with thousands of coastal communities
B) It has no coastline
C) It has no forests
D) It's located far from the ocean

escape.text: Which practice BEST helps mitigate climate change in the Philippines?

choices.label: A) Planting mangroves and trees to absorb CO₂, plus using renewable energy
B) Cutting down forests for more farmland
C) Using more coal power plants
D) Increasing fossil fuel imports
